newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KPW clears all 15 NFIs for public trade.
newsitem.headline: Polish KPW clears all 15 NFIs for public trade.

text.p: The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) on Thursday cleared all 15 National Investment Funds (NFI) in the country's mass privatisation programme for public trade, the KPW's spokeswoman said.
"The KPW on Thursday approved for public trade shares of all 15 National Investment Funds," Beata Stelmach told Reuters.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

The 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme will have the opportunity to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse around mid-year.
Earlier on Thursday deputy treasury minister Ewa Freyberg told Reuters that the ministry wanted the units to be exchangeable into shares in NFIs from May 12 until the end of 1998.
Bourse president Wieslaw Rozlucki has said he envisions the units trading along with the funds on the bourse for a significant period of time.
